title: The orbit thesaurus
teaches: the orbit structure as a computed thesaurus, and the size of the frontier

asserts.statement: The six marks are complete WITH RESPECT TO SYMMETRY ORDER: every order the corpus uses is either a mark's own or is produced by composition.
asserts.derivation: Iterated superposition-with-rotation reaches every C_n, verified by construction for n=2..8 from the C1 Angle alone. Triangle (C3) and the hexagram (C6) are therefore produced, not posited. Closure was also tested and does NOT reach C3 -- a chevron closes to an isoceles triangle, which is C1.
asserts.scope: Covers symmetry order only. Does NOT establish that every figure the corpus draws is reachable -- matching an order is weaker than being the same figure. Two figures are now known unreachable, for two different reasons: the Spiral wants scaling (spiral-requires-scaling) and the teardrop wants a curved join (teardrop-reachability, F123). Neither wants a seventh mark.

carries_undetermined.statement: The teardrop ('Life', Angle+Curve fused) is NOT reachable by close() composed with the attested operators. Exactly-one-corner figures do not occur in that space at all.
carries_undetermined.derivation: 23,424 close() expressions over the six marks: all five attested binary operators, reflect_pair and close as unary steps, sub-expressions nesting one deep on either side, close permitted at any position. 20,142 are closed and enclose area. None has exactly one corner -- the corner-count distribution runs 0:427, 1:NONE, 2:630, 3:2864, and upward. Nearest approach to a constructed teardrop is 0.326 Hausdorff against a same-figure tolerance of 0.073. The cause is structural: close() joins the free ends with a straight chord, and a chord meets two symmetrically-built ends either tangentially at both or at neither, so corners arrive in pairs. Permitting a curved join does produce single-cornered convex figures, which locates the missing capability as the join rather than a missing mark.
carries_undetermined.given: close() joins with a straight chord, and composition nests one deep. A close() that curved would change the answer; depth is bounded by enumeration cost, not by principle.
carries_undetermined.success_condition: Enumerate close() composed with binary operators. This is a scope gap in the search, not evidence of unreachability.
carries_undetermined.scope: Settles reachability, not meaning. Says nothing about whether the corpus intends the teardrop as a primitive rather than a composite.

carries_undetermined.statement: The Spiral is not reachable by any attested operator, and the reason is not a missing scale parameter: it needs MODULATION -- varying a parameter along a mark's own extent -- which is a different operator family from placement.
carries_undetermined.scope: Measured over the 186 enumerated depth-2 combinations, not proved for all compositions. Margin is 0.111 and the nearest case is a near-degenerate stroke. TWO EARLIER INVARIANTS FAILED and are kept on the record: curvature-per-sample (spiral measured 0.95, flat, indistinguishable from a circle) and radial monotonicity (0.967 vs 0.927, contaminated by component stacking order).

combination_space.note: Orbits are the thesaurus: combinations producing the same figure up to rotation and reflection are synonyms. An orbit with no recorded meaning is UNDETERMINED, not free to fill. `combinations` is exact; `orbits` is a quotient taken at a calibrated tolerance and is 89-94 across the interval that calibration licenses -- cite it as a central value, never as an exact count. See the-orbit-count-is-tolerance-bounded.
